lessons.title: Enterprise Architecture
lessons.html:
Java EE Application Architecture

Java EE builds scalable enterprise applications using layered architecture and containers.

Core Layers:

  • Presentation: JSF, JSP, Servlets
  • Business: EJB, CDI beans
  • Persistence: JPA/Hibernate
  • Integration: JMS, JCA
// 3-Tier Architecture Example
@WebServlet("/user")
public class UserServlet extends HttpServlet {
    @Inject UserService userService;
    
    protected void doGet(HttpServletRequest req, HttpServletResponse resp) {
        List<User> users = userService.findAll();
        req.setAttribute("users", users);
        req.getRequestDispatcher("/users.jsp").forward(req, resp);
    }
}

Practice Exercises:

  1. Modify the code example to handle edge cases
  2. Write a test case for the main functionality
  3. Refactor the code to improve performance or readability

Key Takeaways:

  • Understanding the fundamental concepts is crucial for advanced topics
  • Always consider edge cases and error handling in production code
  • Practice with real-world examples to solidify your knowledge

lessons.title: MicroProfile Config & Health
lessons.html:
MicroProfile Configuration and Health Checks

MicroProfile adds cloud-native features to Java EE including external configuration and health probes.

Configuration:

@ApplicationScoped
public class AppConfig {
    @Inject
    @ConfigProperty(name = "app.name", defaultValue = "MyApp")
    private String appName;

    @Inject
    @ConfigProperty(name = "db.url")
    private String dbUrl;

    @Inject
    @ConfigProperty(name = "max.connections", defaultValue = "20")
    private int maxConnections;

    @Inject
    @ConfigProperty(name = "features.preview", defaultValue = "false")
    private boolean previewEnabled;
}

// Custom config source
@ApplicationScoped
public class VaultConfigSource implements ConfigSource {
    @Override
    public Map<String, String> getProperties() {
        return Map.of("db.password", vault.readSecret("db/password"));
    }

    @Override
    public String getValue(String key) {
        if (key.equals("db.password")) {
            return vault.readSecret("db/password");
        }
        return null;
    }

    @Override
    public String getName() { return "VaultConfigSource"; }
}

Health Checks:

@Health
@ApplicationScoped
public class DatabaseHealthCheck implements HealthCheck {
    @Inject
    private DataSource dataSource;

    @Override
    public HealthCheckResponse call() {
        HealthCheckResponseBuilder builder = HealthCheckResponse.named("database");
        try (Connection conn = dataSource.getConnection()) {
            if (conn.isValid(5)) {
                return builder.up().withData("type", conn.getMetaData().getDatabaseProductName()).build();
            }
            return builder.down().build();
        } catch (SQLException e) {
            return builder.down().withData("error", e.getMessage()).build();
        }
    }
}

Practice Exercises:

  1. Create a health check for external API connectivity
  2. Implement config sources for different environments
  3. Add readiness and liveness probes for Kubernetes

Key Takeaways:

  • External configuration enables environment-specific settings
  • Health checks enable automated recovery in containers
  • ConfigSource abstraction supports any backend

lessons.title: JPA Performance Tuning
lessons.html:
Optimizing JPA Queries

JPA performance issues often come from N+1 queries and inefficient fetching strategies.

Fetch Strategies:

@Entity
public class Post {
    @OneToMany(mappedBy = "post")
    @BatchFetch(size = 20)
    private List<Comment> comments;

    @ManyToOne(fetch = FetchType.LAZY)
    @JoinColumn(name = "author_id")
    private User author;

    @ElementCollection
    @CollectionTable(name = "post_tags")
    @Fetch(FetchMode.SUBSELECT)
    private Set<String> tags;
}

// Entity graph for dynamic fetching
@NamedEntityGraph(
    name = "Post.detail",
    attributeNodes = {
        @NamedAttributeNode("author"),
        @NamedAttributeNode(value = "comments", subgraph = "comments")
    },
    subgraphs = {
        @NamedSubgraph(name = "comments", attributeNodes = @NamedAttributeNode("author"))
    }
)
@Entity
public class Post { /* ... */ }

Query Optimization:

// JOIN FETCH to avoid N+1
TypedQuery<Post> query = em.createQuery(
    "SELECT DISTINCT p FROM Post p " +
    "LEFT JOIN FETCH p.author " +
    "LEFT JOIN FETCH p.comments c " +
    "LEFT JOIN FETCH c.author " +
    "WHERE p.published = true",
    Post.class
);

// Pagination with count query
Query countQuery = em.createQuery(
    "SELECT COUNT(p) FROM Post p WHERE p.published = true"
);
long total = (Long) countQuery.getSingleResult();

// Stateless session for batch processing
StatelessSession session = em.unwrap(Session.class).getSessionFactory().openStatelessSession();
ScrollableResults<Post> posts = session.createQuery("FROM Post", Post.class).scroll();
while (posts.next()) {
    processPost(posts.get());
}

Practice Exercises:

  1. Profile JPA queries with SQL logging
  2. Add batch fetching to a one-to-many relationship
  3. Implement read-only queries for better performance

Key Takeaways:

  • FetchType.LAZY is the default for to-many relationships
  • JOIN FETCH loads associations in a single query
  • Batch fetching reduces query count for collections

lessons.title: Jakarta Security & OAuth2
lessons.html:
Modern Security with Jakarta EE

Jakarta Security provides authentication, authorization, and identity stores for enterprise applications.

Security Configuration:

@ApplicationScoped
public class SecurityConfig {
    @Inject
    private SecurityContext securityContext;

    public boolean hasPermission(String resource, String action) {
        return securityContext.isCallerInRole("admin") ||
               securityContext.isCallerInRole(resource + "_" + action);
    }
}

// Custom IdentityStore
@ApplicationScoped
public class DatabaseIdentityStore implements IdentityStore {
    @PersistenceContext
    EntityManager em;

    @Override
    public CredentialValidationResult validate(Credential credential) {
        UsernamePasswordCredential login = (UsernamePasswordCredential) credential;
        User user = em.find(User.class, login.getCaller());
        if (user != null && verifyPassword(login.getPasswordAsString(), user.getPasswordHash())) {
            return new CredentialValidationResult(user.getId().toString(),
                user.getGroups().stream().map(Group::getName).collect(Collectors.toSet()));
        }
        return CredentialValidationResult.INVALID_RESULT;
    }

    @Override
    public Set<ValidationType> validationTypes() {
        return Set.of(ValidationType.VALIDATE);
    }
}

JWT Token Authentication:

@RequestScoped
public class JwtService {
    @Inject
    @ConfigProperty(name = "jwt.secret")
    private String secret;

    public String generateToken(User user) {
        return Jwts.builder()
            .setSubject(user.getId().toString())
            .claim("email", user.getEmail())
            .claim("roles", user.getRoles())
            .setIssuedAt(new Date())
            .setExpiration(Date.from(Instant.now().plus(24, ChronoUnit.HOURS)))
            .signWith(getKey())
            .compact();
    }

    public Claims validateToken(String token) {
        return Jwts.parserBuilder()
            .setSigningKey(getKey())
            .build()
            .parseClaimsJws(token)
            .getBody();
    }

    private Key getKey() {
        return new SecretKeySpec(secret.getBytes(), SignatureAlgorithm.HS256.getJcaName());
    }
}

Practice Exercises:

  1. Implement role-based access control on REST endpoints
  2. Add OAuth2 login with a social provider
  3. Create a custom identity store with two-factor auth

Key Takeaways:

  • IdentityStore abstracts authentication source
  • JWT provides stateless authentication
  • Security constraints protect URL patterns

lessons.title: Batch Processing with JSR 352
lessons.html:
Enterprise Batch Processing

Jakarta Batch provides a framework for large-scale batch processing with chunking and partitioning.

Batch Job Definition:

<job id="importUsers" xmlns="http://xmlns.jcp.org/xml/ns/javaee" version="1.0">
    <step id="step1">
        <chunk item-count="100">
            <reader ref="userFileReader"/>
            <processor ref="userValidationProcessor"/>
            <writer ref="userDatabaseWriter"/>
        </chunk>
        <partition>
            <mapper ref="filePartitionMapper"/>
        </partition>
        <end on="FAILED"/>
        <next on="COMPLETED" to="summaryStep"/>
    </step>
    <step id="summaryStep">
        <batchlet ref="importSummaryBatchlet"/>
    </step>
</job>

Batch Components:

@Named
public class UserFileReader extends AbstractItemReader {
    private BufferedReader reader;
    private int count;

    @Inject
    private JobContext jobContext;

    @Override
    public void open(Serializable checkpoint) throws Exception {
        String file = jobContext.getProperties().getProperty("input_file");
        reader = new BufferedReader(new FileReader(file));
        reader.readLine(); // skip header
        if (checkpoint != null) {
            count = (Integer) checkpoint;
            for (int i = 0; i < count; i++) reader.readLine();
        }
    }

    @Override
    public Object readItem() throws Exception {
        String line = reader.readLine();
        if (line != null) {
            count++;
            return parseUser(line);
        }
        return null;
    }

    @Override
    public Serializable checkpointInfo() throws Exception {
        return count;
    }
}

Practice Exercises:

  1. Create a batch job for monthly report generation
  2. Implement partitioned processing for large files
  3. Add restart capability with checkpoint save

Key Takeaways:

  • Chunk processing handles large datasets efficiently
  • Checkpoints enable job restart from failures
  • Partitioning enables parallel processing

lessons.title: WebSockets with Jakarta EE
lessons.html:
Real-Time Communication

Jakarta WebSocket provides annotations for creating WebSocket endpoints in enterprise applications.

Server Endpoint:

@ServerEndpoint("/chat/{room}")
@ApplicationScoped
public class ChatEndpoint {
    private static final Map<String, Set<Session>> rooms = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();

    @OnOpen
    public void onOpen(Session session, @PathParam("room") String room) {
        session.getUserProperties().put("room", room);
        rooms.computeIfAbsent(room, k -> ConcurrentHashMap.newKeySet()).add(session);
        broadcast(room, "User joined: " + session.getId());
    }

    @OnMessage
    public void onMessage(String message, Session session) {
        String room = (String) session.getUserProperties().get("room");
        String sender = session.getId();
        broadcast(room, sender + ": " + message);
    }

    @OnClose
    public void onClose(Session session) {
        String room = (String) session.getUserProperties().get("room");
        Set<Session> roomSessions = rooms.get(room);
        if (roomSessions != null) {
            roomSessions.remove(session);
            broadcast(room, "User left: " + session.getId());
        }
    }

    @OnError
    public void onError(Session session, Throwable error) {
        Logger.getLogger(ChatEndpoint.class.getName()).log(Level.SEVERE, null, error);
    }

    private void broadcast(String room, String message) {
        Set<Session> roomSessions = rooms.get(room);
        if (roomSessions == null) return;
        roomSessions.stream()
            .filter(Session::isOpen)
            .forEach(session -> {
                session.getAsyncRemote().sendText(message);
            });
    }
}

Practice Exercises:

  1. Build a real-time notification system
  2. Add WebSocket authentication with JWT
  3. Implement a collaborative editing endpoint

Key Takeaways:

  • @OnOpen/OnMessage/OnClose handle lifecycle events
  • Sessions are thread-safe with ConcurrentHashMap
  • AsyncRemote sends messages without blocking
